meta.topStoryHeadline: Obama Presidential Center Opens on Juneteenth with Historic Black Artist Commissions
meta.topStorySummary: One of the largest single commissions of Black artists at a major public institution — Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Rashid Johnson, Lorna Simpson, Jeffrey Gibson, and more. Opening weekend is free to the public in Chicago's Jackson Park.
executiveSummary: This week's defining story: the Obama Presidential Center opens on Juneteenth with one of the most ambitious collections of Black artist commissions ever assembled for a single public institution.

Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater begins its final run of the season at BAM under new Artistic Director Alicia Graf Mack — only the fourth in the company's 67-year history. Four nights only, starting June 4.
On the policy front: a federal judge has blocked the Kennedy Center's planned closure and ordered Trump's name removed from the building within two weeks. The NSO remains in institutional peril.

events.title: Joy Guidry: Five Prayers
events.description: Experimental ambient performance moving through jazz, minimalism, opera, ballet, blues, and gospel. 75 minutes, no intermission. One of the most original experimental musicians working in New York.

events.title: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater at BAM
events.description: The inaugural New York season under Artistic Director Alicia Graf Mack — only the fourth in the company's 67-year history. World premiere of Hymn, with a libretto by Anna Deavere Smith. Revelations closes every performance.

events.title: Gateways Brass Collective Free Concert
events.description: The only all-Black professional brass quintet in the United States, performing free outdoors. The kind of event members will not see on mainstream roundups.

events.title: Chief Xian aTunde Adjuah — Blue Note Jazz Festival
events.description: One of the most original jazz musicians working — a descendant of Mardi Gras Indians, deeply rooted in New Orleans Black musical tradition. Four consecutive nights in an intimate room of roughly 200.

events.title: Jazz at Lincoln Center: Folklore LIVE Vol. 2 — Etienne Charles
events.venue: Appel Room, Jazz at Lincoln Center
events.description: Etienne Charles addresses the music and traditions of Anglophone Afro-Caribbean culture. Part of Jazz at Lincoln Center's Mother Africa season.

events.title: Willie Cole: Mind, Body, and Soul
events.description: A new body of work from one of the most formally inventive Black American artists working. Sculptures and assemblages that draw on domestic objects as cultural and racial symbols.

events.title: Harlem Chamber Players: Concert in the Sugar Hill Hope Garden
events.description: A community-rooted chamber ensemble bringing classical music to Harlem. Free outdoor concert in a Harlem community garden.

events.title: Ledisi for Dinah — SummerStage (Blue Note Jazz Festival)
events.description: Grammy-winning vocalist Ledisi performs her tribute album honoring blues icon Dinah Washington. Opening night of SummerStage's 40th anniversary season.

events.title: Step Afrika!: The Migration — Reflections on Jacob Lawrence
events.description: Step Afrika! transforms Jacob Lawrence's Migration Series into percussive, embodied performance. A meditation on the Great Migration of Black Americans to the North.

events.title: Jasmine Hearn: Memory Fleet: Beloved, Let's Cross
events.description: World premiere. An episodic archive centered on the lived experience of Black people who shaped one choreographer's artistic life. Post-show Stay Late Conversation on June 12.

events.title: Brian Blade & The Fellowship Band — Blue Note
events.description: One of the most original drummers in contemporary jazz. The Fellowship Band is rooted in his Louisiana upbringing, gospel, and post-bop tradition. Four nights in a room of 200.

events.title: Jazz at Lincoln Center: Soul of Brazil
events.venue: Rose Theater, Jazz at Lincoln Center
events.description: The JLCO performs works of Moacir Santos, legendary Black Brazilian composer, with bandolinist Hamilton de Holanda. A deep dive into the African-Brazilian roots of jazz.

events.title: Schomburg Centennial Festival + Black Feminist Shorts
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: The Schomburg turns 100. A full day of literary programming, the Black Comic Book Festival, and a screening of Black feminist shorts. A generational cultural event in Harlem.

events.title: Studio Museum: Artist-in-Residence Open Studios
events.description: First look at works-in-progress from the 2026 cohort: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, and Taylor Simmons. An intimate entry point to the next generation of artists of African descent.

events.title: Brandee Younger — Blue Note Jazz Festival
events.description: Harpist, composer, and producer whose work sits at the intersection of classical training and contemporary Black music. A Blue Note set is the right room for her.

events.title: La Cage aux Folles (Encores!) — All-Black Cast
events.description: Billy Porter and Wayne Brady lead. Directed by Tony nominee Robert O'Hara. Timed with NYC Pride. An all-Black cast revival of the beloved musical.

events.title: Omari Wiles / Les Ballet Afrik — Lincoln Center
events.description: Legendary Black dancer and choreographer Omari Wiles brings his company Les Ballet Afrik to Lincoln Center's outdoor plaza.

events.title: Book Launch: Never Tell a Black Girl How to Black Girl — Amena Brown
events.description: Amena Brown launches her new essay collection at the Afro-Latine feminist bookstore in Crown Heights. Published by Tiny Reparations Books. The week of Juneteenth.

events.title: Oh Sankofa! — Lincoln Center Summer for the City
events.venue: Hearst Plaza / Damrosch Park, Lincoln Center
events.description: Fifth annual Juneteenth celebration by Carl Hancock Rux. Music, dance, and spoken word woven with African and African American folklore. Starts outdoors, moves to the park.

events.title: Ogemdi Ude: MAJOR — Danspace Project
events.description: A celebration of majorette dance — physicality, history, and interiority of Black femme teams whose movement combines showmanship, undulation, groove, and strength. RSVP required.

events.title: Studio Museum: Juneteenth Community Day
events.description: A full day of workshops, curator talks, and performances at the newly opened Studio Museum building. One of the best ways to spend Juneteenth in New York.

events.title: Bronx Book Festival
events.description: S.A. Cosby and Tiffany D. Jackson headline. A full day outdoors in the Bronx centering Black authors — the literary equivalent of DanceAfrica in community scale.

events.title: ABTKids, hosted by Misty Copeland
events.description: Misty Copeland hosts a one-hour introduction to ballet for families. A meaningful point of entry to classical ballet, centering a Black cultural figure.

events.title: Classical Theatre of Harlem: Othello
events.venue: Richard Rodgers Amphitheater, Marcus Garvey Park
events.address: 122nd St & Mount Morris Park West, Harlem
events.description: Annual Uptown Shakespeare in the Park. Othello, free, outdoors in Harlem. Shakespeare produced by and for a Harlem community, at a park that carries its own history.

events.title: Sanford Biggers: Homecoming — Socrates Sculpture Park
events.address: 32-01 Vernon Blvd, Long Island City, Queens
events.description: Sanford Biggers is one of the most formally ambitious Black artists working today. Major public sculpture work in Long Island City. Always open, always free. Verify opening date.

exhibitions.title: Willie Cole: Mind, Body, and Soul
exhibitions.description: Sculptures and assemblages drawing on domestic objects as cultural and racial symbols — from one of the most formally inventive Black American artists working.

exhibitions.title: Jeffrey Gibson — Monumental Bronze Sculptures
exhibitions.description: Monumental bronze sculptures at the Metropolitan Museum. Closing imminently — act now.

exhibitions.title: Venice Biennale 2026: In Minor Keys
exhibitions.description: The posthumous curatorial vision of Koyo Kouoh — the first African woman to curate the Biennale — realized at Giardini, Arsenale, and across Venice.

news.title: Obama Presidential Center Opens on Juneteenth with Historic Black Artist Commissions
news.summary: The Obama Presidential Center opens in Chicago's Jackson Park on Juneteenth with site-specific commissions from Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Rashid Johnson, Lorna Simpson, Jeffrey Gibson, and more. Akunyili Crosby created the first official portrait of Barack and Michelle Obama. Opening weekend is free to the public.
news.detail: One of the largest single commissions of Black artists at a major public institution in recent memory. The Juneteenth opening is a deliberate cultural statement. Multiple artists Soirée follows are represented here.

news.title: Alvin Ailey Closes Its Season at BAM Under New Artistic Director Alicia Graf Mack
news.summary: Only the fourth Artistic Director in the company's 67-year history, Graf Mack leads her inaugural New York season. The role is now endowed at $10 million following a landmark gift. Four nights at BAM, ending June 7.

news.title: Federal Judge Blocks Kennedy Center Closure, Orders Trump Name Removed
news.summary: A federal judge ruled that only Congress has the authority to close or rename the Kennedy Center. Rep. Joyce Beatty's trustee voting rights were restored. The NSO remains in institutional peril. Black composer Valerie Coleman premieres a new concerto there this week.

news.title: Venice Biennale 2026 Opens Carrying Out Koyo Kouoh's Posthumous Vision
news.summary: Kouoh — the first African woman ever selected to curate the Venice Biennale — passed away in May 2025. Her team is realizing her vision for 'In Minor Keys' at the Giardini, Arsenale, and across Venice.

news.title: Joe Turner's Come and Gone — Taraji P. Henson's Broadway Debut, Directed by Debbie Allen
news.summary: August Wilson's classic is on Broadway at the Barrymore Theatre, directed by Debbie Allen. Playing at 87.9% capacity. Over $7.3 million in total gross. Members should act soon.

news.title: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing — Largest Retrospective to Date Opens at BAMPFA
news.summary: Over 20 major works spanning fifty years of sculpture, installation, video, and performance. The Berkeley Art Museum opened the most comprehensive survey of Hassinger's career on June 6.

appointments.name: Alicia Graf Mack
appointments.role: Artistic Director, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater
appointments.description: Only the fourth person to hold this role in 67 years. Former Ailey principal dancer and renowned educator. The position is now endowed at $10 million.

appointments.name: Lisa Funderburke
appointments.role: Director & CEO, Newark Museum of Art
appointments.description: One of the few Black directors at a mainstream US art museum. Howard University alumna. A potential Soirée partner institution.

appointments.name: J'Nai Bridges & Kwamé Ryan
appointments.description: Houston Grand Opera's 'Intelligence' by Jake Heggie. Bridges' second Grammy. Ryan conducts. Two Black artists at the summit of classical recording.

appointments.name: Koyo Kouoh
appointments.description: First African woman selected to curate the Venice Biennale. Her vision — 'In Minor Keys' — is being realized by her team. Open through November 2026.
